This application aims to enhance the safety and precision of gene-editing therapies.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models

bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.

Ollama currently serves a large developer community, boasting 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The speed improvement is achieved through Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when benchmarked with Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using its MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and reduced memory usage for models.
The updated engine also contributes to higher quality outputs from the language models.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new model architecture.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, offering an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability for these AI agents to run entirely on the user's local hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and adoption.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and speed.
The core value proposition is running AI tools entirely on the user's own device.

stories.title: This is the world's most advanced robotic servicing satellite—that we know about
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: The article discusses a highly advanced robotic servicing satellite, indicating significant progress in space technology.
Robotic servicing satellites represent a major step toward in-orbit maintenance and repair capabilities.
The complexity of these systems highlights advanced engineering challenges in the aerospace industry.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses the limitation of 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in handling complex 3D spatial reasoning tasks.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries into VLMs.
Employs Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to inject high-level geometric priors into the model for enhanced 3D awareness.

stories.title: GraphVid: Interactive Graph-Controllable Video Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: GraphVid addresses the challenge of precise multi-object interaction control in video generation.
It overcomes limitations of text prompts and trajectory-based controls that struggle with scene complexity and occlusion.
The method introduces a graph-based approach for flexible and precise multi-subject control in video synthesis.

stories.title: Beyond Sycophancy: Structured Resistance and Compliance in LLM Moral Reasoning
stories.author: Bernard Koch
bullet_points: The research addresses the limitations of simply reducing LLM sycophancy by focusing on structured resistance and compliance.
The study investigates how LLMs distinguish between incorporating external perspectives and maintaining independent moral judgment.
Model judgment revision is found to be structured along three dimensions related to the resistance-compliance process.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces OpenForgeRL, an open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
Addresses the challenge of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code/Codex) using open infrastructure.
Enables multi-turn reasoning and tool use for agents across diverse environments without proprietary harness limitations.

stories.title: 3D-Aware VLMs with Implicit and Explicit Geometries
stories.author: Gongjie Zhang
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in current 2D Vision-Language Models (VLMs) regarding 3D spatial understanding.
Introduces VLM-IE3D, a unified framework that integrates both implicit and explicit 3D geometries.
Utilizes Implicit Geometry Tokens (IGTs) to enhance the 3D spatial awareness of VLMs using RGB video data.

stories.title: X$^3$-OPD: Distilling Reasoning into Large Audio-Language Models via On-Policy Alignment
stories.author: Tao Jin
bullet_points: Addresses the gap in deep logical reasoning within large audio-language models (ALMs) compared to text-based LLMs.
Proposes X$^3$-OPD, a cross-modal on-policy distillation framework to transfer reasoning skills.
The method uses a powerful text teacher model to guide the training of an audio-language student model.

stories.title: OpenForgeRL: Train Harness-native Agents in Any Environment
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: OpenForgeRL is a new open-source framework designed to train AI agents end-to-end.
It addresses the difficulty of training agents that rely on complex, stateful inference harnesses (like Claude Code or Codex) using standard open infrastructure.
The framework enables training harness-native agents across diverse and complex environments.

stories.title: DONDO: Open w2v-BERT Speech-Recognition Base Models for African Languages
stories.author: Paul Azunre
bullet_points: Introduction of DONDO, a new family of open, permissively licensed ASR base models.
The models support twenty-seven language varieties across several African nations (e.g., Ghana, Nigeria, Kenya).
DONDO is built upon the w2v-BERT 2.0 self-supervised speech encoder, utilizing read speech from religious texts for training.

stories.title: Windowed-MTP: Removing the Full-Context Draft-KV Tax at Million-Token Context
stories.author: Alagappan Valliappan
bullet_points: The paper addresses a critical performance bottleneck in speculative decoding when using Multi-Token-Prediction (MTP) draft heads.
The issue arises because MTP draft heads incur a linear cost with context length due to full attention over the KV cache.
The proposed 'Windowed-MTP' aims to mitigate this 'Full-Context Draft-KV Tax' to maintain efficiency at million-token contexts.

stories.title: Claude Opus 5
stories.author: alvis
bullet_points: Announcement of Claude Opus 5, indicating a new iteration or version of Anthropic's flagship large language model.
The source points directly to the official system card, suggesting a formal release or detailed technical documentation is available.
This represents a significant update in the competitive landscape of frontier AI models.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings improved performance and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for advanced AI features within Claude Code.
The new capabilities include the implementation of subagents for complex task decomposition.
Web search functionality has been added, enhancing the model's ability to access real-time information.

stories.title: After backlash, Meta pauses plan to ‘rate limit’ its smart glasses
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Meta has paused its plan to implement a $20 monthly subscription fee for its smart glasses feature.
The feature in question allows users to hear each other more clearly and operates locally on the glasses.
The pause follows public backlash against the proposed monetization strategy.

stories.title: Meta just created a moderation nightmare for its smart glasses
stories.author: Mia Sato
bullet_points: Meta's smart glasses are facing significant public backlash regarding privacy concerns.
The devices are being misused by bad actors to film and prank unsuspecting strangers.
There are specific reports of women being targeted and filmed without consent for social media content.

stories.title: Qualcomm is about to raise prices and that’s bad news for everyone
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Qualcomm plans to implement double-digit price increases for its products.
The price hikes are scheduled to take effect for shipments after September 1st.
The company cites rising supplier costs and ongoing component shortages as the reason for the increases.

stories.title: Anthropic's Opus 5 is about token efficiency, not a capability leap
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic's Opus 5 update emphasizes token efficiency over radical capability gains.
The article suggests that current, more cost-effective AI models are often sufficient for practical use cases.
This signals a trend in the industry prioritizing operational efficiency and cost reduction alongside performance.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: The paper introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
It addresses a limitation in existing methods by moving beyond mere 'sufficiency' to incorporate 'necessity' in explanations.
TimePNS aims to prevent the assignment of high importance to spurious subsequences that don't drive the model's actual decision.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning abilities when presented with different modalities (text vs. diagram) for the same problem.
The study, titled MIRROR, suggests that different views expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning pathways in VLMs.
This highlights a current limitation in multimodal AI, where strong text reasoning does not guarantee strong visual reasoning, and vice versa.

stories.title: Expanding Flow Maps
stories.author: Pranam Chatterjee
bullet_points: Introduces Expanding Generative Flows (EFlows) to address limitations in existing flow-based generative models.
EFlows allow for generation across distributions of increasing dimensionality by augmenting the state with conditional noise.
The research aims to overcome constraints related to fixed dimensions or fixed sequence lengths in current generative models.

stories.title: Beyond Sufficiency: Time Series Explanation with Counterfactual Necessity
stories.author: Weiru Liu
bullet_points: Introduces TimePNS, a new framework for explaining time-series classifiers.
Addresses a limitation in existing methods by moving beyond mere 'sufficiency' to incorporate 'necessity' in explanations.
Aims to prevent spurious subsequences from being over-weighted in model explanations, aligning with counterfactual reasoning.

stories.title: Graph Learning on Ensembles of Cyclic Peptides: An Investigation of Molecular Ensemble Modeling
stories.author: Maxim Secor
bullet_points: Introduces EnsembleEGNN, a foundation model designed to handle molecular conformational ensembles rather than single structures.
The model utilizes Equivariant Graph Neural Networks (EGNN) to encode individual conformers, followed by a Set Attention Block for ensemble pooling.
It is pre-trained on CREMP, a dataset specifically focused on cyclic peptide ensembles, indicating application in structural bioinformatics/drug discovery.

stories.title: MIRROR: Learning from the Other View for Multi-Modal Reasoning
stories.author: Xuezhe Ma
bullet_points: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) show inconsistent reasoning capabilities across different input modalities (text vs. visual diagrams).
The study, MIRROR, suggests that different views (text, diagram, combined) expose complementary, yet sometimes conflicting, reasoning pathways in VLMs.
This highlights a key weakness in current VLMs: their inability to robustly handle visual reasoning tasks, even when equivalent textual representations exist.

stories.title: The Boundaries of Automation: A Theory of Persistent Human Participation
stories.author: Iryna Gurevych
bullet_points: The paper challenges the prevailing assumption that human involvement in AI is solely due to current system limitations.
It shifts the focus from 'how far automation can extend' to identifying the conceptual limits of automation.
The research posits that human participation may remain necessary even when AI systems achieve high levels of capability.

stories.title: MedGame: Storytelling Gamification Empowered by Large Language Models for Medical Education
stories.author: Qi Dou
bullet_points: Introduces MedGame, a framework that uses LLMs to transform static clinical cases into interactive, decision-centered storytelling games for medical education.
Addresses a limitation in current LLM medical tools, which often only handle localized tasks like Q&A rather than full learning trajectories.
Employs a dual-engine design, including a Medical Narrative Designer, to structure complex clinical scenarios into executable game narratives.

stories.title: GS-Agent: Creating 4D Physical Worlds With Generative Simulation
stories.author: Chuang Gan
bullet_points: The research introduces 'GS-Agent' to generate dynamic, physically realistic 4D worlds from natural language prompts.
It addresses a key limitation in current generative models: ensuring physical plausibility and controllability in simulated environments.
This work aims to automate the traditionally manual and labor-intensive process of creating complex computer graphics.

stories.title: Artificial Epanorthosis: Why large language models overuse a classical rhetorical figure, and how to mitigate it
stories.author: Federico Boggia
bullet_points: LLMs exhibit a systematic overuse of 'epanorthosis,' a classical rhetorical self-correction technique.
The overuse is attributed to training data rich in promotional prose and RLHF rewarding emphatic phrasing.
The study suggests the left-to-right generation process contributes to this rhetorical pattern.

stories.title: What, Where, and How: Disentangling the Roles of Task, Language, and Model in Code Model Representations
stories.author: Piotr Wilam
bullet_points: The research investigates how different language models (Qwen2.5-Coder-7B vs. DeepSeek-Coder-V1-6.7B) represent code concepts across different programming languages (Python vs. Rust).
It employs a 2x2 design to disentangle the influence of the specific task, the programming language, and the underlying model architecture on code representations.
The study measures a comprehensive inventory of grammatical concepts (58 for Python, 57 for Rust) to determine if representations are consistent across the tested configurations.

stories.title: Agentic coding without the cloud: evaluating open-weight large language models on longitudinal data preparation tasks
stories.author: David Bann
bullet_points: Addresses the privacy and governance limitations of using cloud-based LLMs for sensitive data tasks.
Proposes using locally deployable, open-weight LLMs as an alternative for secure, on-premise AI agent evaluation.
Introduces an open-source framework to evaluate the effectiveness of AI agents in longitudinal data preparation tasks.

stories.title: Android May Soon Restrict On-Device ADB
stories.author: shscs911
bullet_points: Android is reportedly planning to restrict On-Device ADB (Android Debug Bridge).
This change suggests a move towards tighter security and reduced developer access on consumer devices.
The news is circulating on Hacker News, indicating developer and tech community interest.
